newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of China to launch first HK$ FRCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China to launch first HK$ FRCD issue.

text.p: Bank of China has mandated China Development Finance Co to arrange a HK$2 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue, bankers said Thursday.
They said the facility has a final maturity of five years with no put or call options.
This is the first Hong Kong dollar issue for Bank of China.

The bank last year yanked a HK$5.0 billion deal after Moody's Investors Service downgraded its rating to Baa1, which made the issue ineligible for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.

At that time, eligibility for LAF required that issues must be HK$1.0 billion or more in size and carry ratings of A2 and Single-A by Moody's Investors Service and Standard and Poor's Corp, respectively.
But in May 1996, the HKMA said that it would accept ratings of the Japan Bond Research Institute (JBRI) and IBCA.
The change meant that many issuers, notably Bank of China, now are eligible for LAF status.
Last year's suspended Bank of China issue was hugely oversubscribed--it launched at HK$1.0 billion--and bankers said a new issue is likely to be similarly well received.
